newsitem.title: USA: IBM jumps again ahead of Q4 earnings.
newsitem.headline: IBM jumps again ahead of Q4 earnings.

text.p: Shares of International Business Machines Corp jumped again on Tuesday ahead of its fourth quarter earnings, which are due for the first time in recent memory after the U.S. stock market closes.

Analysts said there is no particular negative significance in IBM's reporting after the close, except that the computer giant is trying to avoid the drastic swings in its stock price that have occurred during its analysts' conference call, which IBM hosts after the earnings are released.
Traders and analysts also said that they are not hearing any so-called "whisper" numbers ahead of its earnings report.
"Whisper" numbers refer to unofficial estimates that Wall Street traders and analysts are speculating about, which usually differ from the published numbers on Wall Street.
According to First Call, the published consensus estimate for IBM is $3.88 a share in the fourth quarter, with a range of $3.13 to $4.32.
"I don't think there is any real signal of a problem," said Gary Helmig, a SoundView Financial analyst, who has a buy rating and a near-term price target on IBM of $180 by June.
IBM's shares were up two to 169 in active trading, approaching the stock's all-time high of 175, which it reached in August, 1987, before the October 1987 stock market crash.

"People are looking for IBM to be a little better than expected," said Daniel Ries, a Nomura Securities analyst, adding that IBM has a tremendous upgrade cycle with its new mainframes in the fourth quarter.
Shares of Compaq Computer Corp were also trading higher, up 2-1/4 to 78, ahead of its fourth quarter earnings. Compaq will report Wednesday, before the U.S. stock market opens.
